  Regular Meeting

  ITEM 2:  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT CUP-21-17
  • 2133 West Valley Boulevard
  • Request: This is an application for a Conditional Use Permit to allow
  an on-premise alcoholic beverage license (Type 41) for the sale of beer
  and wine in conjunction with meal service in an existing restaurant
  located in the Valley Boulevard Corridor Specific Plan (VSP) zone.
  (This item is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act)
  • Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 21-30 approving
  Conditional Use Permit CUP-21-17, subject to the Conditions of
  Approval.
  • Principal Planner Lam provided Staff’s presentation and indicated
  an amendment to Condition of Approval PD2.
  • Public Comments: There were none.
  • Commissioner Comments:
  President Gardea inquired if any food purchases will be provided in
  to-go containers.
  Commissioner Wang inquired if there were any physical
  modifications required under Code for such uses.

  MOTION:
  •  Moved to approve Conditional Use Permit CUP-21-17 with an amendment
  to Condition of Approval PD2.
  •  Moved by Commissioner Ho. Seconded by Commissioner Sahu.
  •  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  Roll Call Vote:  9-0

ITEM 4:  VARIANCE VAR-21-16
  • 242 East Main Street
  • Request: This is an application for a Variance to reduce the number of
  required on-site parking spaces for a tattoo establishment in a 1,280
  square foot lease space that was previously a beauty salon use on an
  approximate land area of 17,000 square feet located in the CBD
  (Central Business District) zone and DRD (Downtown Revitalization
  Overlay District). (This item is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act)
  • Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 21-31 approving
  Variance VAR-21-16, subject to the Conditions of Approval.
  • Principal Planner Lam provided Staff’s presentation.
  • Public Comments: There were none.
  • Commissioner Comments:
  President Gardea noted that the Police Department Conditions of
  Approval were heavily weighted towards regulating the sale and
  service of alcohol. He also asked if the Applicant was present to
  discuss a possible reduction in the business hours. Principal Planner
  Lam replied that the Police Department was being cautious and took a
  preventative stance against alcohol being present on the property. The
  Applicant was not available, however, Principal Planner Lam stated
  that the request in front of the Commission was a Variance for a
  parking reduction and that the nexus between the business hours and
  parking was tenuous.
  Commissioner Sahu commented that it was his observation that the
  nearby parking structure was not heavily used.
MOTION:
  •  Moved to approve Variance VAR-21-16.
  •  Moved by Commissioner Sahu. Seconded by Commissioner Olson.

ITEM 3:  PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT PD-21-30, CONDITIONAL
  USE PERMIT CUP-21-12 AND VARIANCE VAR-21-11

  •  2505 West Valley Boulevard
  •  Request: This is an application for a Planned Development Permit,
  Conditional Use Permit and Variance to construct an approximate 753
  square foot exterior covered patio for outdoor dining for an existing
  restaurant on an approximate land area of 21,531 square feet located at
  2505 West Valley Boulevard in the VSP (Valley Boulevard Corridor
  Specific Plan) zone. A Variance is requested to reduce the number of
  required on-site parking spaces. (This item is exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act)
  •  Recommended Action: 1. Continue the public hearing on Planned
  Development Permit PD-21-30, Conditional Use Permit CUP-21-12 &
  Variance VAR-21-11 to a date certain. 2. Alternatively, direct Staff to
  return to the next scheduled Planning Commission with Resolution No.
  21-19, to deny Planned Development Permit PD-21-30, Conditional
  Use Permit CUP-21-12 & Variance VAR-21-11 to establish an
  approximately 753 square foot exterior covered patio for outdoor
  dining for an existing restaurant with less than the required parking
  spaces on an approximate land area of 21,531 square feet located at
  2505 West Valley Boulevard in the VSP (Valley Boulevard Corridor
  Specific Plan) zone in the City of Alhambra.
  •  Associate Planner Scott Quyle provided Staff’s presentation.
  •  Omar Hernandez, Applicant, provided a brief presentation.
  •  Public Comments: There were none.

  4
  11/15/2021
   •  Commissioner Comments:
  Vice President Garcia stated that he sensed tension between the
  Applicant and Staff. He also added that a deficiency of 5 parking
  spaces did not warrant denial of the project. He verified with Staff that
  there were other possible options that would not require off-site
  parking. He stated this was a good project for the area and he would
  be supportive of the project.
  Commissioner Sahu clarified procedural matters since there was an
  absence of 2 Variance applications. He wanted to hear from the
  Applicant the reasons the other alternatives were rejected or considered
  cost prohibitive. He viewed the project as an expansion that required
  additional parking spaces per Code. He stated that he recognized the
  City’s flexibility in trying to find a solution to the problem, however,
  he did not see any flexibility by the Applicant. He also asked the
  Applicant to explain why all but one option was unfeasible.
  Commissioner Ho stated that the project was a big improvement to
  the property. He inquired on the number of staff. He concurred with
  the Applicant’s position that some of the options were cost prohibitive.
  He suggested adding 2 Conditions of Approval to require property
  owner approval for use of off-site parking lots and for the Applicant to
  apply for the 2 additional Variances.
  Commissioner Wang pointed out the difference between this item and
  Item #4 that also requested a parking Variance, but that application had
  the benefit of the multi-level public parking garage nearby. She
  inquired as to how customers would know to park at the remote parking
  lots. She did not agree that some options were cost prohibitive and
  concurred with Commissioner Sahu’s opinion that the Applicant has
  not been flexible with the request.
  Commissioner Pham was concerned with the reduced back-up space
  for some of the parking spaces and the potential for accidents. She
  asked if there were any accident reports filed from the parking lot.
  Commissioner Tsujii verified that two additional Variances were
  needed if the project were to be approved. He also verified that the
  property owners’ approvals were required for the parking agreements.
  Commissioner Juarez inquired to what extent did the Applicant reach
  out to the other property owners.
  President Gardea inquired if reducing the dining area was an option.
  Staff replied that it was an option that the Applicant flatly rejected.

RECESS:  The Planning Commission took a brief recess from 8:51 PM to 9:00
  PM.

  Principal Planner Lam reported that during the recess, Staff verified
  that the property owners of the 2 remote parking lots had mailing
  addresses in Bakersfield and Tustin.

  Vice President Garcia was of the opinion that 28 on-site parking

   spaces were sufficient.

  MOTION:
  •  Moved to approve Planned Development Permit PD-21-30, Conditional
  Use Permit CUP-21-12 and Variance VAR-21-11 with the minimum
  number of parking spaces reduced to 28 spaces and with the need of 2
  additional Variances.
  •  Moved by Vice President Garcia. President Gardea clarified that a
  continuance was in order.
  •  Vice President Garcia amended the motion to continue Planned
  Development Permit PD-21-30, Conditional Use Permit CUP-21-12 and
  Variance VAR-21-11 to a date uncertain. Seconded by Commissioner Ho.
  •  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  Roll Call Vote:  6-3

  Noes:  Sahu, Tsujii, Wang
